steps.text: 19:46 P.M. \ Clear
Rhodes Island Landship, Operator Rest Area, Bar

steps.name: Operator Barty
steps.text: How many cards?

steps.name: Operator Dylan
steps.text: I'll take two.

steps.name: Operator Chard
steps.text: Let me see... I'll have one.

steps.name: Operator Barty
steps.text: Noir Corne?

steps.name: Noir Corne
steps.text: I'm out.

steps.name: Operator Dylan
steps.text: Luck's not smiling today, eh, bro?

steps.name: Noir Corne
steps.text: Aw, man, I bet it's because I took the wrong mask out! Dammit.

steps.name: Operator Barty
steps.text: Been busy enough recently, huh? I heard you were helping ops with simulation training, all on top of your run of field missions.

steps.name: Noir Corne
steps.text: Nah, an extra shift once in a while's no big.

steps.name: Noir Corne
steps.text: And I mean, I like training with all the newcomers. Youngsters with a love for life.

steps.name: Operator Dylan
steps.text: Haven't you always been pretty popular, Noir?

steps.name: Operator Dylan
steps.text: When I first arrived, I saw your mask, and I thought 'old, serious mentor type.' Swear I didn't even dare talk to you. Who knew you'd take me for drinks right after training, eh...

steps.name: Noir Corne
steps.text: Wait, old mentor? Am I really that old? If you don't take that back, your next round's not on me!

steps.name: Operator Dylan
steps.text: As a bro! I mean as a solid, dependable bro.

steps.name: Operator Dylan
steps.text: Hey, bro. I'll take another card.

steps.name: Operator Barty
steps.text: You know, Dylan, if you got out more and spent less time crammed in your cockpit, you'd be more popular too.

steps.name: Operator Dylan
steps.text: Forget it, goofing off in there suits me. If Noir didn't invite me, I wouldn't have wanted to come out.

steps.name: Operator Chard
steps.text: ...I'm more of the hiding sort too.

steps.name: Operator Chard
steps.text: Last time I saw Noir Corne and the Doctor show up together, I ducked behind a wall on sheer reflex.

steps.name: Operator Barty
steps.text: Haha, that's just you overreacting, isn't it?

steps.name: Operator Chard
steps.text: I can't help it. After we got back from Lungmen, I had nightmares a couple straight days in a row.

steps.name: Operator Chard
steps.text: It takes a lot of guts to keep working with Dr. Kal'tsit watching, and then when I saw the Doctor and all the others in the squad at the time, and the herd showing up in front of us...

steps.name: Operator Chard
steps.text: That was... a terrifying scene.

steps.name: Operator Dylan
steps.text: Man, that's just rough, bud. What about you, Noir? You went too, right?

steps.name: Noir Corne
steps.text: I'm good enough.

steps.name: Noir Corne
steps.text: But that battle was pretty intense. Can't blame Chard. Even I'm still a little stressed about it.

steps.name: Operator Chard
steps.text: ...I'll have another glass. Talking about this made me break a sweat.

steps.name: Operator Dylan
steps.text: Yeah, me too, gimme the... Water of Life with vanilla soda!

steps.name: Operator Dylan
steps.text: Not gonna drink, Noir?

steps.name: Noir Corne
steps.text: I'll pass.

steps.name: Operator Barty
steps.text: Yo, you're worried Yato's gonna tell you off, huh? Never seen you hold back before.

steps.name: Noir Corne
steps.text: Hey, hey. I'm older than you guys. Lay off the wisecracks.

steps.name: Noir Corne
steps.text: —I'll give you the double-demon killer!

steps.name: Operator Dylan
steps.text: C'mon, you're just bluffing again. You're the worst actor every time you do this, y'know!

steps.name: Noir Corne
steps.text: (Scratches mask) You serious?

steps.name: Noir Corne
steps.text: Dammit. Don't they say masks hide your expression, make it easier to scare people?

steps.name: Operator Dylan
steps.text: Don't forget tone of voice. The moment you start bluffing, you sound super tense! It's like telling everyone what you're about to do. Anyone'd figure out the act, y'know?

steps.name: Noir Corne
steps.text: Oh? I guess my acting still needs some work, then.

steps.name: Noir Corne
steps.text: Oh, well. This next one's on me. You guys drink happy.

steps.name: Operator Chard
steps.text: ...If you say so. Give me another one.

steps.name: Operator Barty
steps.text: Ease off, Chard. I don't want a repeat of you at the toilet bowl hurling and crying, yelling your daughter and ex-wife's names.

steps.name: Operator Barty
steps.text: That last celebration dinner, if Noir Corne didn't carry you back to your place, you would've embarrassed yourself in front of the Doctor and Dr. Kal'tsit all night long.

steps.name: Operator Chard
steps.text: (Groan)

steps.name: Operator Dylan
steps.text: You gotta lay off him now. Keep going and he'll pass out clutching the whole bottle, haha.

steps.name: Noir Corne
steps.text: Chard's having a hard time. Went through a rough battle, returned living, and couldn't even tell the people that mattered about it. I know how that hits. You guys stop joking about him.

steps.name: Operator Chard
steps.text: Thanks... s-see, I was genuinely scared... I wish I could be like you, Noir Corne, I've never seen you freeze up in any situation...

steps.name: Noir Corne
steps.text: I've just been round the block a few more times. Everyone'll get used to it after a while.

steps.name: Operator Chard
steps.text: Once I got back, I couldn't help picturing that scene. Those kind of conditions, that sort of place... if you left me to do anything alone right there, I wouldn't have made one step forward. Wouldn't have dared fall one step back.

steps.name: Operator Chard
steps.text: Dr. Kal'tsit told me to think of my daughter. She said, if we won, I'd have a chance to see her again.

steps.name: Operator Chard
steps.text: *Sigh*... I already know the thing, doctor. No matter if I die there or not, whether I get to see her again isn't my place to say.

steps.name: Noir Corne
steps.text: I feel you.

steps.name: Operator Chard
steps.text: The reason I... the reason I could keep walking was because she said we could win. I chose... *hic* to listen to that.

steps.name: Operator Chard
steps.text: Then when we got back, I saw her and the Doctor again, and I was ashamed like nothing else. In that one moment, I was actually doubting we could win!

steps.name: Noir Corne
steps.text: I'm not saying this to be nice, Chard—that mindset? I've thought like that too.

steps.name: Noir Corne
steps.text: I've been through a lot of conflicts before. Used to just fight one battle to make it to the next, and when all was said and done, who won and who lost had nothing to do with a small fry like me.

steps.name: Noir Corne
steps.text: Feeling like you can't win is normal. When you can't beat them, run, because your life's what's important. If you can keep just making it through the days, your job's done.

steps.name: Operator Barty
steps.text: It's totally normal. Plenty of mercenaries think that way.

steps.name: Operator Barty
steps.text: I used to run a security company outside, and people got the services they paid for, no other questions asked.

steps.name: Noir Corne
steps.text: Then coming to Rhodes Island, same as the boss here, my mentality began to change.

steps.name: Noir Corne
steps.text: I've been on plenty of missions with the Doctor. I slowly got to thinking, if we can win, and keep on winning at it, that's actually pretty slick!

steps.name: Noir Corne
steps.text: Like that, I passed each day, hauling my weight on the battlefield, and now I'm even pumped for training. I'm practically keeping up with the young kids.

steps.name: Operator Chard
steps.text: I wanna win too. I've always believed in what all the doctors are doing.

steps.name: Operator Chard
steps.text: I wanna see my daughter, even if rationally, the odds are almost nothing. I'm still not gonna give up on them.

steps.name: Noir Corne
steps.text: Hey, hey, that's the spirit! Good on you!

steps.name: Noir Corne
steps.text: Rhodes Island always needs guys like us, after all. Is it our fault, really, we're not as strong, or we can hesitate, or we can get scared?

steps.name: Noir Corne
steps.text: The Doctor told me to 'defend your own position,' and I did it. I've earned the pay, and I've earned the Doctor's trust.

steps.name: Noir Corne
steps.text: And you were with Dr. Kal'tsit all the way to the end. You gonna tell me she chewed you out for it after coming back?

steps.name: Operator Chard
steps.text: No. She... she actually commended me.

steps.name: Noir Corne
steps.text: You see? Just like I said, right?

steps.name: Operator Chard
steps.text: Yeah. I think you've actually helped me get past it a little.

steps.name: Operator Chard
steps.text: But I still don't have the kind of good mentality you do. At the most, I won't hide behind a pillar next time I see the Doctor. Might even say hello by myself. See, you know, there's a whole lot of long-time ops who make the Doc sound mighty impressive.

steps.name: Operator Chard
steps.text: We were on the same mission last time, sure... urp. But in the end, we didn't get to talk much.

steps.name: Operator Chard
steps.text: Thinking about it, the Doctor sure as hell wouldn't remember me now... ugghhh...

steps.name: Operator Barty
steps.text: Alright, Chard, I can safely say you're drunk again.

steps.name: Noir Corne
steps.text: Lemme ease you up, buddy.

steps.name: Noir Corne
steps.text: Better?

steps.name: Operator Chard
steps.text: Phew... yeah, better...

steps.name: Noir Corne
steps.text: I just wanna say, it doesn't mean someone's difficult when they cover up their face. You know that looking at me, don't you?

steps.name: Noir Corne
steps.text: You can see for yourself the way the Doctor is, now we're all off the battlefield.

steps.name: Noir Corne
steps.text: Once you're familiar, you'll realize the Doctor's not much different from us. There's two eyes and a mouth in there, a slacker, someone who makes mistakes, who worries about the schedules of every single department on this landship every day.

steps.name: Operator Dylan
steps.text: Yeah, now that you mention it, the Doc might be coming along on my next field mission soon!

steps.name: Operator Dylan
steps.text: That's a hell of a good chance. Right this moment, I'm even more curious about the Doctor than I am about what's under your mask, Noir!

steps.name: Noir Corne
steps.text: Haha... that's good, yeah.

steps.name: Operator Barty
steps.text: Are you okay, Chard? Should we keep going?

steps.name: Operator Chard
steps.text: *cough*... Yeah, let's keep going. I'm much better now.

steps.name: Operator Barty
steps.text: What's your hand?

steps.name: Operator Dylan
steps.text: Straight flush, yuccas!

steps.name: Operator Dylan
steps.text: Looks like you've lost again, Noir!

steps.name: Operator Barty
steps.text: If we keep drinking at this rate, we're gonna run the liquor cabinet dry. We need some different stakes.

steps.name: Operator Dylan
steps.text: Then... if Noir loses again, he's gotta take his mask off!

steps.name: Noir Corne
steps.text: Hey, hey, that's not gonna fly. It's not like I'm not willing, it's just you guys might be disappointed.

steps.name: Operator Dylan
steps.text: Yeah, the more you deflect, the more curious I get! I've been so curious, I've even dreamt it in my nightmares...

steps.name: Operator Chard
steps.text: What did you dream?

steps.name: Operator Dylan
steps.text: Noir finally took off his mask, and underneath was another mask. And it was just one after another, kept going forever.

steps.name: Operator Chard
steps.text: That's a nightmare for sure. I've got goosebumps now.

steps.name: Noir Corne
steps.text: Oh yeah, that's a pretty solid dream. I like it.

steps.name: Noir Corne
steps.text: If I could put on a bunch of masks in one go, I wouldn't have to worry about which one to wear every morning.

steps.name: Operator Dylan
steps.text: Come on, shatter the mystery, bro... I don't wanna dream about you every night!

steps.name: Operator Barty
steps.text: Naughty, haunting Dylan's dreams. Looks like sometimes secrets are charming too.

steps.name: Noir Corne
steps.text: I'm not kidding you guys, I don't have much of a secret. If you actually wanna look, I can—

steps.name: Operator Dylan
steps.text: Uh, nah!

steps.name: Operator Dylan
steps.text: Noir, you just stay as you are, bro, I think that's best. I'm worried you'd throw me for a loop if you actually had the mask off.

steps.name: Operator Barty
steps.text: So, same as always, then?

steps.name: Noir Corne
steps.text: Man, you guys. You wanna hear me tell stories again?

steps.name: Operator Dylan
steps.text: C'mon, bring it on! Your stories are the best part of playing cards.

steps.name: Noir Corne
steps.text: Hm, lemme think. Last time we got to...

steps.name: Operator Chard
steps.text: It was a rainy evening, and a mom and her kid were hiding in a... ruined temple? Then an Oni ran into them.

steps.name: Operator Dylan
steps.text: Wow, Chard, that's a killer memory you've got! Yeah, it was all like a scary movie. Then what happened?

steps.name: Noir Corne
steps.text: —The Oni was there to kill.

steps.name: Operator Dylan
steps.text: Kill? And I thought the Oni'd be a good guy.

steps.name: Noir Corne
steps.text: Right then, he was just an Oni someone told to go killing, so he went killing.

steps.name: Operator Dylan
steps.text: Sounds like he's got it pretty tough...

steps.name: Noir Corne
steps.text: The Oni knocked the mom out, but when he had the daughter nabbed, it hit him she was just seven or eight, scared so bad she couldn't even scream.

steps.name: Noir Corne
steps.text: The Oni thought to himself, 'it's for the mission, that's how it is,' getting ready to slaughter her.

steps.name: Noir Corne
steps.text: That's when he noticed his strike being blocked by a blade.

steps.name: Operator Dylan
steps.text: That's cool!

steps.name: Noir Corne
steps.text: Yeah, it was real cool, even I thought so. Uh, I mean, the Oni in the story thought so.

steps.name: Noir Corne
steps.text: The light off that blade was real bright that night. The Oni couldn't help but fall back a little.

steps.name: Operator Dylan
steps.text: I get it, this was the hero coming to save the mom and kid, right?

steps.name: Noir Corne
steps.text: Ha, the Oni was thinking that too.

steps.name: Noir Corne
steps.text: He reckoned, if he couldn't win the fight, then forget it. Not like he was interested in killing anyone anyway. Act like he got hurt, treat the mission as a failure, and it's not like anyone would give him a hard time for it.

steps.name: Noir Corne
steps.text: Only then did the Oni realize... the one who blocked his attack was another Oni.

steps.name: Operator Dylan
steps.text: Huh? Why'd that Oni come save the family, then?

steps.name: Noir Corne
steps.text: At the time, he couldn't figure it out either. The weirdest thing was, seemed the other Oni was a whole other clan's lackey. Her head and his head were both out for the same thing, that girl's life.

steps.name: Operator Chard
steps.text: Seriously? She held you off just so she could get her own kill?

steps.name: Noir Corne
steps.text: The Oni guessed the same thing. He threw some hands with the other Oni, which led him to realize she actually wanted to save the kid.

steps.name: Noir Corne
steps.text: So he asked her, what is it you wanna do?!

steps.name: Noir Corne
steps.text: And she told him, she didn't wanna do anything. She just didn't wanna hurt another innocent person.

steps.name: Noir Corne
steps.text: That stunned the Oni. He never once figured that was an option they could take.

steps.name: Operator Barty
steps.text: Hey, sounds like he was a nice, soft guy... uh, soft Oni.

steps.name: Noir Corne
steps.text: Yeah. He decided then and there, he'd let the girl go.

steps.name: Operator Dylan
steps.text: Because he was moved by the other Oni?

steps.name: Noir Corne
steps.text: Ha... and maybe because he wasn't a match for her.

steps.name: Operator Barty
steps.text: Giving up the mission yourself, that amounts to desertion. The powers on both their sides wouldn't let a traitor off easy, would they?

steps.name: Noir Corne
steps.text: Yeah, so he came to the conclusion, he could only desert with the other Oni.

steps.name: Operator Dylan
steps.text: Man, fleeing together to the ends of the world! This turned from a horror story into a romance story.

steps.name: Noir Corne
steps.text: It wasn't that romantic, was it? Trying to run away's not an easy thing... they got hurt together, they fell ill together. Had more than a couple close scrapes with death.

steps.name: Noir Corne
steps.text: Not to mention, the other Oni couldn't stand being in sunlight. And nowhere's quick to trust you when you're always wearing a mask.

steps.name: Noir Corne
steps.text: The Oni was obsessed, because masks were obviously pretty sweet, so he spent some crazy effort getting a whole pile of them.

steps.name: Operator Dylan
steps.text: A pile of masks?

steps.name: Noir Corne
steps.text: Yeah, that was hard-earned as hell. Every mask was passed down by a different clan for a millennium, and had secret powers unbeknownst to anyone...

steps.name: Operator Barty
steps.text: This is getting wilder by the second.

steps.name: Operator Dylan
steps.text: What kind of secret powers is a mask gonna have?

steps.name: Noir Corne
steps.text: For example, you wear it and you're unaging and immortal. You get a huge strength boost or something.

steps.name: Noir Corne
steps.text: Yeah, take that day, for instance. The Oni got his hands on the most fearsome mask of them all, and it came at a huge price. Almost cost him his life.

steps.name: Noir Corne
steps.text: The other Oni was worried as hell for him. With all the guys chasing him, he did what he could in the moment, and put the mask straight on!

steps.name: Noir Corne
steps.text: And in that instant, sand and stone came flying up, and every last enemy went pale—

steps.name: Noir Corne
steps.text: And the Oni yelled in this huge voice, 'I've broken the limits!'

steps.name: Noir Corne
steps.text: And then in a huge blast of spiritual energy, he sent every last bad guy packing.

steps.name: Operator Dylan
steps.text: Huh? What? That's way too sloppy for an ending! C'mon, Noir, every time you finish up, your stories just get more and more bizarre...

steps.name: Noir Corne
steps.text: Well, hey, looks like I won, huh?

steps.name: Operator Dylan
steps.text: Huuuh?! I got way too absorbed in the story...

steps.name: Operator Chard
steps.text: Same here...

steps.name: Operator Barty
steps.text: Same all around, huh.

steps.name: Operator Dylan
steps.text: I see how it is! This is your special technique, isn't it, Noir?

steps.name: Noir Corne
steps.text: Hey, hey, it's more effective than trying to bluff people out.

steps.name: Operator Dylan
steps.text: Augh, I still wanna hear more stories about the two Oni...

steps.name: Operator Dylan
steps.text: The one from before with the Oni challenging ten generals in a row on the night of a snowstorm, that was amazing!

steps.name: Noir Corne
steps.text: Yeah, we'll leave it for next time. Looks to me like Chard's eyes are almost gluing shut.

steps.name: Noir Corne
steps.text: When you're out from your field mission, then we can go for drinks again.

steps.name: Noir Corne
steps.text: Hey, that's the Doctor, isn't it?

steps.name: Operator Dylan
steps.text: What? I was just staring at the cards—I didn't even notice!

steps.name: Operator Dylan
steps.text: Must've heard everything we were just talking about...

steps.name: Operator Chard
steps.text: I... *cough* *cough* *cough*... I feel dizzy as hell...

steps.name: Operator Barty
steps.text: Too late to act drunk, Chard.

steps.name: Noir Corne
steps.text: Doctor, I never imagined you'd drop in at the bar.

options: Amiya suggested I come over and relax.
Is my camouflage module on the fritz?

steps.name: Operator Chard
steps.text: Whaddaya nudging me for, you guys...

steps.name: Operator Chard
steps.text: *cough*... Doctor, been ages since... uh, good evening!

steps.name: Operator Chard
steps.text: *huff*...

options: Good evening, Operators Chard, Dylan, Barty, Noir Corne.

steps.name: Operator Chard
steps.text: Doctor, you... you actually remember all our names?!

steps.name: Noir Corne
steps.text: Your memory's still as good as ever, Doctor.

steps.name: Noir Corne
steps.text: Getting into your mountain of paperwork, and remembering all our personnel's names on top of that, it's not easy. Doctor, watch you don't get worn out.

options: It's just what I ought to do.

steps.name: Operator Barty
steps.text: Doctor, we're about to pack up right now. We'll give you some peace and quiet.

steps.name: Operator Dylan
steps.text: Uh-huh. Doctor, see you on the field mission!

steps.name: Operator Dylan
steps.text: We're out, Chard, what are you stuck to the ground for?

steps.name: Operator Chard
steps.text: Huh? Yeah... *cough*, see you, Doctor.

steps.name: Noir Corne
steps.text: Doctor, you don't mind if I sit down here, right?

steps.name: Noir Corne
steps.text: Just now, we were meeting up after work, drinking and shooting the breeze. Must've been a comedy show for you.

steps.name: Noir Corne
steps.text: They still don't really know what to make of you. But I know it well. You're fun, interesting, and a real good person.

steps.name: Noir Corne
steps.text: It's your command, y'know, that lets guys like me find their proper position in a scene all tossed about head to tail.

steps.name: Noir Corne
steps.text: And my position—is right here.

steps.name: Noir Corne
steps.text: I'll go for anything. It's all tasty.

steps.name: Noir Corne
steps.text: How about a drink with me, Doctor? A glass every now and then's no big deal.
